question: Resuming from the verified checkpoint_300 with the cont400 configuration, but replacing the fixed 40-row Y72 rehearsal (memorized to near-zero loss) by a fresh pool in which every rehearsal row is presented exactly once: does Y72 HOLD on the 600-set (no 375-type collapse) while X64 progresses?

motivation.diagnosis: docs/Y72FIX2_CONT400_SWING_DIAG.md (commit b9926d6): after the 40 replay rows were memorized (CE 0.0057 at 350), the clipped replay pull fell to 0.15 (share 0.19, 16/25 updates < 0.1) in 351-375 and its held-out transfer was weak (0.035); X drove the step and Y72 fell 504 -> 396; the replay rows then degraded and pulled Y72 back to 573 at 400 while X64 gave back 48/83 exact.
motivation.control: the cont400 run (prereg/y72fix2_cont400.json, results ad0bf9b): same start, plan, clip and replay weight; Y600 504/396/573, X64 exact 46/124/82, tokens at 400 1658; verdict FAIL_HOLD_PROGRESS

design.only_change_vs_control: the source of the 2 replay rows per update. Control: rows (2s+j) % 40 of the fixed 40-row rehearsal artifact (sha256 abd8d94d...), each row presented 5 times in 301..400. Treatment: rows 2(u-301)+j (j = 0,1) of the fresh pool F200 at update u = 301..400, so every one of the 200 pool rows is presented exactly once and no replay row is ever repeated.

fresh_pool_F200.generator: the existing Experiment-Y generator (experiments/y/make_corpus_Y.py, sha256 3a78a791711364070e0f67eb22e4e11f206d93792f285b2e982154e2b4be5c2f), functions extracted verbatim exactly as in prereg/y72_heldout_v2/gen_y72_heldout.py; the extraction reproduces the shipped D72 unseen rows exactly (log)
fresh_pool_F200.seed_policy: new role bases 20264600 + 100k (k = 0..4) + distance 72, one gen_rows(72, 40, seed) call per block; none of these seeds appears as a literal anywhere in the generator repo or this repo (overlap_pool.json)
fresh_pool_F200.ban_set: 11189 payloads: the 600-set's 600, every train_Y payload (all geometries train + unseen incl. the 200-set, gap probes), the 40 rehearsal rows' 200, probe_Q and train_T2/V/W/X; plus the running used set
fresh_pool_F200.deterministic: regenerated twice: identical canonical and payload-list sha256
fresh_pool_F200.order: pool row index = 2*(u-301)+j; block k serves updates 301+20k .. 320+20k
fresh_pool_F200.refresh_rule_beyond_400: not part of this experiment; a longer run would need new blocks with new bases 20265100 + 100k under the same ban rule, registered before use

disjointness_from_eval.declared: NO overlap with any evaluation set. Pool payloads vs the 600-set, the 200-set, the Y72 train 8 rows and the 40 rehearsal rows: 0 shared payloads, 0 exact rows, 0 shared 16-byte and 32-byte windows; no pool payload occurs anywhere in the 600-set rows (overlap_pool.json). Pool and 600-set share only the generator and its corpus filler source, exactly as the 600-set shares them with the original training rows.
disjointness_from_eval.why_not_overlap: drawing rehearsal from the 600-set would make the hold gate measure memorization; the pool is a disjoint draw from the same distribution instead

design.why_it_is_not_memorized: each pool row is seen once, so at its presentation its loss is a held-out loss. Measured at the five control checkpoints (rows not yet seen): pool CE / held-out 200-set CE = 0.88, 0.88, 0.95, 0.85, 0.78 at 300/325/350/375/400, vs 0.061, 0.050, 0.054, 0.075, 0.070 for the 40-row set. The signal falls only as far as Y72 generalization itself falls.
design.clip_and_lambda_kept: kept. With fresh rows 0.25*|g_rep| exceeds 0.5 on 88/80/76/100/32% of probed updates at the 300/325/350/375/400 states, so the replay contribution is mostly at the 0.5 cap (parity with X); lambda would not change a bound update, and changing tau would add a second change and confound the attribution
unchanged: resume from checkpoint_300 (sha256 5df9a3f8bcf04dbeac6b15d96a312e3fa3b425aef60639a603ece3c19fea45a3) with the same full v2 restore and the same exact-restoration check as prereg/y72fix2_cont400.json
SliceAdam LR 3e-4, expert-selection union, per-task clip 0.5 on gx and on 0.25*gy
evaluation code, held-out sets incl. the 600-set (canonical sha256 16ff53a839c5c68e2230fe4f96e794f11d7ff7f885cac3e184e4f4770f3ee71b), no reseed
updates 301..400, evals and complete checkpoints at 325, 350, 375, 400; one run, stop at 400

P(c g/|g|); ratios are reported, absolute first-order values are not calibrated

manipulation_checks_nongating.purpose: verify from the run's own per-update clip record that the signal behaved as designed; reported next to the verdict, never change it
manipulation_checks_nongating.M1_no_starved_window: in each 25-update window (301-325, 326-350, 351-375, 376-400) the median replay contribution alpha_y*|g_y| is >= 0.10 (control: 0.095, 0.202, 0.072, 0.217)
manipulation_checks_nongating.M2_not_memorized: in each window the median replay loss is >= 0.005 (control: 0.0044, 0.0079, 0.0039, 0.0038); the probe's lowest fresh-pool median was 0.0058 at the 400 state, so M2 can fail if Y72 generalization becomes very good, which is then reported as such
manipulation_checks_nongating.M3_presentation_once: every pool row index 0..199 presented exactly once (structural)

expected_effect.what_is_supported: a mechanism-level prediction: the treatment removes the replay starvation that preceded the control's collapse (contribution median 0.5 vs 0.069 at the 350 state; 1 vs 13 of 25 updates below 0.1) and its direction is better aligned with held-out Y72 (cos 0.09-0.14 vs 0.05-0.07 at 300-375). Predicted 600-set outcome: no checkpoint collapse (each >= 432) and a sum >= 1440.
expected_effect.what_is_NOT_supported: a calibrated effect size in 600-set segments. The probe is first-order and counterfactual (control states), there is one control trajectory, and the parent run slid 524 -> 496 over updates 276-300 with a replay share of 0.27 (contribution median 0.13), i.e. without a starved window like the control's, so steady replay alone has not been shown to hold Y72. No segment gain is claimed.
expected_effect.detectable_contrast: the gate separates the two outcomes that matter with high power: the control's observed profile 504/396/573 passes R with probability 0.000; a hold at the 300 level (496 flat) passes with 0.96-0.97; a single dip to 440-460 with the other checkpoints near 500-520 passes with about 0.77; a parent-like slide 480/464/448 passes with 0.03-0.04
expected_effect.x64_direction: expected to be HARDER than in the control: the fresh signal's first-order X64 cost is 1.8-8.9x the control rows' at 300-375 (and costs at least as much X per unit of Y benefit at 3 of 4 states: 0.98/1.42/2.50 vs 0.67/1.39/1.57), because the held-out Y72/X64 conflict (cosine about -0.8) is unchanged. The control gained no X64 tokens (1665 -> 1658).

noise_math.x64: token gain SD 21 (sqrt2 x 15): P(tokens >= 1723 | true gain g) = 0.003 at 0, 0.04 at 20, 0.20 at 40, 0.51 at 58, 0.86 at 80, 0.999 at 120; exact >= 44 at all three checkpoints (SD 6, independent approx.) = 0.15 at a flat 44, 0.64 at 50, 0.92 at 55, 0.99 at 60

R.basis: judgment, not computed: the starvation that preceded the control's only R failure is absent at every probed state, but the treatment trajectory is unmeasured and the parent slid without starvation

A.basis: judgment, not computed: the control made no token progress with a weaker replay pull; the fresh signal pulls harder along the same conflict axis

pass_probability.most_likely_named_outcome: FAIL_PROGRESS (R passes, A fails) or FAIL_HOLD_PROGRESS
pass_probability.plain_statement: This design tests whether a non-memorizable rehearsal signal removes the Y72 collapse. It is not expected to make X64 progress; a SUCCESS is unlikely. FAIL_PROGRESS would confirm the mechanism and isolate the remaining limit as the structural Y72/X64 conflict.
